changes.text: 这份记述出自《南方》作者欧内斯特·沙克尔顿的第一人称自述，他是这支队伍的队长。经过一段乘船航程后，他和全队困在象岛：粮食有限，有人冻伤，而且象岛上根本不会有人来搜寻他们。口粮按足额只够全队吃五个星期。减量可以撑三个月，或许还能靠海豹和海象补一些，但沙克尔顿不敢把信心全押在这上面：海滩上的海兽似乎都走了，冬天近了。燃料主要靠海兽脂肪，存量里有三只海豹和两张半带脂肪的兽皮。初步估量形势后，他决定全队每天只吃一顿热食。

This account comes from the first-person narrative of Ernest Shackleton, author of South and leader of this party. After a boat journey, he and his men were stranded on Elephant Island: food was limited, a man was frostbitten, and there was no chance at all of any search being made for them there. At full ration the food would last the whole party five weeks. Cut back, it could be spread over three months, and would probably be supplemented to some extent by seals and sea-elephants — but Shackleton dared not count on that with full confidence. The animals seemed to have deserted the beach and winter was near. They were mainly dependent on blubber for fuel, and their stocks included three seals and two and a half skins with the blubber attached. After a preliminary survey of the situation, he decided the party must be limited to one hot meal a day.
谁去谁留，从两个要求随行的人说起：以领航见长的沃斯利（Worsley），和后来留在岛上主持队伍的怀尔德（Wild）。两人都意识到必须出海，都要求随行；队长当场告诉怀尔德他必须留下，靠他在自己离开期间把队伍拢住，并交代万一求援失败，春季带人去欺骗岛（Deception Island）。带沃斯利的理由写得很实在：队长对他作为领航员的准确与迅速评价极高，尤其在困难情况下能迅速测出并算出船位。

Who went and who stayed began with two men who asked to come: Worsley, valued as a navigator, and Wild, who would stay on the island to hold the party together. Both realized the attempt must be made, and both asked to accompany him. The leader told Wild at once that he must stay — to hold the party together during the absence and, if the rescue failed, to take the men to Deception Island in the spring. His reason for taking Worsley was practical: "a very high opinion of his accuracy and quickness as a navigator, and especially in the snapping and working out of positions in difficult circumstances".
还需要四个人。队长决定征求志愿者，同时老老实实写明：他心里其实基本知道会选谁——「I pretty well knew which of the people I would select」。克林（Crean）原本被安排留在岛上当怀尔德的帮手，他恳求随行，与怀尔德商量之后，队长答应带上他。挑人的标准也摆在明处：有人不够强壮，担不动船上的活；有人不是熟练水手，在船上派不上用场。

Four more were needed. He decided to call for volunteers while admitting, honestly, that he already knew his choices — "I pretty well knew which of the people I would select". Crean had been slated to stay behind as Wild's right-hand man, but he begged so hard for a place in the boat that, after consulting Wild, the leader promised to take him. The criteria were stated openly: some were not fit for the work the boat would demand, and others, not seasoned sailors, would be of little use aboard.
有人提议把双脚冻伤的布莱克博罗（Blackborrow）带上船，让他尽快得到温暖和庇护。队长否掉了这个提议。记录里给的理由是存活推断：健康的人在船上都难活，重病躺在舱底、动弹不得的人，熬不过必定会遇到的坏天气。

One proposal was to take Blackborrow, the man with the frostbitten feet, so that he could have shelter and warmth as quickly as possible. The leader vetoed it. The record gives survival reasoning: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could not be expected to survive the heavy weather they were sure to encounter.
名单最后定为沃斯利、克林、麦克尼什（McNeish）、麦卡锡（McCarthy）、文森特（Vincent）和队长本人六人。另一件事是加固小船：队长把木匠叫来，请他想办法让小船更耐风浪；木匠先问自己是不是随行的人，听说「Yes」显得相当高兴。他年过五十，身体不算好。

The list closed at six: Worsley, Crean, McNeish, McCarthy, Vincent, and the leader himself. A separate matter was strengthening the boat: the leader called the carpenter and asked whether he could do anything to make the boat more seaworthy; the carpenter's first question was whether he was going along, and hearing "Yes," he seemed quite pleased. He was over fifty and not altogether fit.
木匠拼凑出的骨架很简陋，但足以给一层帆布覆罩打底。帆布冻得硬邦邦，只能先裁好，再在脂肪炉上一英尺一英尺地烤开，才能缝成覆罩，最后钉好、拧紧。覆罩装上后确实给了小船一层安全的样子，可队长心里不踏实，觉得它「bore a strong likeness to stage scenery」——看着像花岗石墙，其实不过是帆布和板条。事后证明，这层覆罩确实顶用。

The framework the carpenter put together was a patched-up affair, but it provided a base for a canvas covering. The canvas came frozen stiff; it had to be cut and then thawed over the blubber stove foot by foot before it could be sewn into a cover, then nailed and screwed into position. The cover did lend the boat an appearance of safety, but the leader felt uneasy that "it bore a strong likeness to stage scenery" — a wall that looks like granite and is in fact no better than canvas and lath. As events proved, the covering served its purpose well.

队长与沃斯利、怀尔德登上临海的岩顶，从比海滩更好的位置察看冰情；外面的浮冰带看来已碎得足够，他决定除非条件不允许，次日早晨乘詹姆斯·凯尔德号（James Caird）出发。浮冰随时可能合拢。决定做出后，队长用当天余下的时间检查船、装备和物资，并与沃斯利、怀尔德商量计划。在象岛坚实陆地上的最后一夜又冷又不舒服。开船前，队长乘小艇上岸，与留守并全权指挥的怀尔德作最后交代：交代万一求援失败他该怎么做，同时几乎把整个局面和行动、决定的范围都交给怀尔德自行判断，「I practically left the whole situation and scope of action and decision to his own judgment」，并告诉他把队伍托付给他，随后向众人道别。升帆解缆向东北而去时，留在岸上的人在海边站成可怜的一小群，背后是岛上冷硬的高地，脚下的海在翻涌；他们挥手，喊了三声欢呼。

Worsley, Wild and the leader climbed to the summit of the seaward rocks to examine the ice from a better vantage-point than the beach offered. The belt of pack outside appeared sufficiently broken, and he decided that, unless conditions forbade it, they would start in the James Caird the following morning. The pack might close at any time. With that decision made, the leader spent the rest of the day looking over the boat, gear and stores, and discussing plans with Worsley and Wild. The last night on the solid ground of Elephant Island was cold and uncomfortable. Before casting off, the leader went ashore for a final word with Wild, who remained in full command: directions for what to do if no help came, and then, in his words, "I practically left the whole situation and scope of action and decision to his own judgment". He told Wild he trusted the party to him and said goodbye to the men. With the jib set and the painter cut, they stood away to the north-east. Those left behind made a pathetic little group on the beach, grim heights at their backs and the sea seething at their feet — but they waved and gave three hearty cheers.

航程中有一次，遇上了队长二十六年海上经历中从未见过的巨浪，与多日来那些白浪翻卷的大浪完全不同。他高喊大家抓紧。船被像软木塞一样抛起、向前甩出，灌进半船水，在重击下颤抖；所有人拼命用随手抓到的容器掏水，十分钟后才觉得船重新有了生命。文森特在过去一周已不再是积极的船员，队长写明难以解释他的垮掉——他是船上体格最强壮的人之一，年轻，在北海拖网船上干过，本该比麦卡锡更能吃苦，而麦卡锡没那么强壮，却总是乐呵呵的。淡水减到每人每天半品脱。带上船的冰块早已用完，装船时一只水桶在浪里被撞裂，渗进了一些海水，喝的水发咸，渴得更厉害；队长不肯增加配给，有人恳求预支第二天的水，也被拒绝：万一风向不利，船可能被吹离海岛，航程拖长许多天。原文感叹，缺水是人所能承受的最严酷的匮乏。5月8日中午12点30分，麦卡锡从云隙中望见南乔治亚的黑色悬崖，距离开象岛整十四天。5月10日，他们驶向一处队长认为必定是哈康国王湾（King Haakon Bay）的大海湾；风向转为从湾内吹出，他们在强风中抢风五次，才穿过礁石进入宽阔的湾口。暮色将近，他们转向海湾南岸一处有礁石护着的小湾。

At one point came a wave beyond anything the leader had met in twenty-six years at sea — a mighty upheaval of the ocean, quite apart from the white-capped seas that had been their tireless enemies for many days. He shouted for everyone to hold on: "It's got us!" The boat was lifted and flung forward like a cork, half-full of water and shuddering under the blow; the men baled with the energy of men fighting for life, and after ten minutes of uncertainty felt her renew her life beneath them. Vincent had for the past week ceased to be an active member of the crew, and the leader could not easily account for his collapse: physically one of the strongest men in the boat, young, with service on North Sea trawlers, he should have borne hardship better than McCarthy, who was not so strong but always happy. The daily water allowance was cut to half a pint a man. The lumps of ice taken aboard were long gone, and the breaker had been slightly stove in during loading, letting in some sea-water, so the brackish water sharpened the thirst; the leader would not raise the allowance or let anyone draw against the morrow's, however he was begged — should the wind turn unfavourable, it might drive them away from the island and lengthen the voyage by many days. Lack of water, the account adds, is the severest privation men can be condemned to endure. At 12.30 p.m. on May 8, McCarthy caught a glimpse of the black cliffs of South Georgia through a rift in the clouds, just fourteen days after leaving Elephant Island. On May 10 they made for a big indentation the leader thought must be King Haakon Bay; with the wind blowing out of the bay, they tacked five times in the strong wind before getting through the reef into the wide mouth of the bay. With dusk approaching, they turned toward a small cove guarded by a reef on the south side of the bay.
还有一处值得留意：记述说他决定征求志愿者，同时心里早有人选。作者提出的一种替代做法是直接点名，省掉征求的形式；但若按记述的叙述顺序读——先写这件事需要向全队详细论证危险和理由，再写决定征求志愿者，最后落名单——这种安排可能让名单更像共识而不是指派。原文没有写明当众论证与征求志愿的实际先后，也没有写明是否确已征求；这只是一种解释，原文也没有说明他为什么这样安排。

One more detail catches the eye: the account says he decided to call for volunteers while already knowing his choices. One alternative would have been simply to name names and skip the formality. But if one reads by the order of the narrative — first that the case had to be argued to the party in some detail, then the decision to call for volunteers, then the settled list — the arrangement may make the list read as consensus rather than assignment. The original does not state the actual order of the arguing and the call for volunteers, nor whether volunteers were in fact called for; this is only one reading, and the original gives no reason for the arrangement.
这套记录只有当事人一个史源，是他事后写下的第一人称自述。文中的对话都带有记述性质：把队伍托付给怀尔德的那句交代、克林恳求随行，都未必是逐字原话。队长自述看队员时信心在增加，那是回忆中的自我描述，不是当时可核实的心理记录。

This record rests on exactly one historical source: a first-person account written after the fact by one of those involved. Its dialogue is reported, not transcribed — the words entrusting the party to Wild, Crean's plea for a place in the boat — and need not be verbatim. The leader's statement that his confidence grew as he looked at the men is retrospective self-description, not a verifiable record of his state of mind at the time.
还有两处要留白。文森特为什么垮掉，队长自己说难以解释，本文不替他补心理。所引片段未给公元年份，这里不做换算；正文的天数只用原文明确写出的出海第六天和离开象岛第十四天，日期照原文写5月8日、5月10日；距离、口粮、水的数字都照原文：八百多英里、三百八十多英里、半品脱。原文是扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文写法。

Two blanks stay blank. Why Vincent collapsed, the leader himself says he could not easily account for, and this piece supplies no psychology for him. The quoted passages give no calendar year, so none is supplied here; the only day counts kept in the text are the sixth day out and the fourteenth day after leaving Elephant Island, both stated explicitly in the original, and dates follow the original: May 8 and May 10; distances, rations and water figures follow the original: over eight hundred miles, over three hundred and eighty miles, half a pint. The source is a scanned, text-recognized print, with occasional garbled words; quotations follow it as printed.
全文只有当事人一个史源（其事后的第一人称自述）；对话与心理均为记述性内容，未必逐字、不可核实；天数只用原文明确写出的出海第六天和离开象岛第十四天，日期照原文写5月8日、5月10日，所引片段未给公元年份，不做换算；距离、口粮、水的数字照原文写法；原文为扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文。

The whole piece rests on a single source — one participant's first-person account written afterwards. Dialogue and psychology are reported rather than transcribed, need not be verbatim, and cannot be verified; the only day counts used are the sixth day out and the fourteenth day after leaving Elephant Island, as stated in the original, dates follow the original (May 8 and May 10), and the quoted passages give no calendar year, so none is supplied; distances, rations and water figures follow the original wording; the source is a scanned print in OCR, with individual words occasionally garbled, and quotations follow it as printed.
先算最坏情形：出去的人不增加留守者的开支，反而少一份开销；给出去的人定明确的时限与物资上限（例如一个月、只带够一个月开销的钱），超时即默认失败；说清楚：之所以冒这个险，只因为确实急需外援；公开征求意愿，但事先想好人选；离开前交代失败时的后手，并把现场判断权交给留守负责人。

Compute the worst case first: the person who goes adds nothing to the burn of those who stay, and in fact removes one salary's worth of cost. Set a hard time limit and a supply cap for the trip (say, a month, carrying only a month of expenses), with silence past the deadline counted as failure. State plainly that the risk is being taken only because outside help is urgently needed. Ask for volunteers in the open, with the choices already thought through. Before leaving, hand over the fallback for failure, and delegate real judgment to the person staying behind.

dispositions.rationale: 开头先交代记述者沙克尔顿是《南方》作者、本队队长，经乘船航程后困在象岛，粮食有限、有人冻伤、无人搜寻；先给五个星期这一比较，海豹与兽皮存量后移；ev 补入 E1、E5。中英同步。

evidence.quote: Blackborrow’s feet, which had been frost-bitten during the boat journey, were in a bad way
there was no chance at all of any search being made for us on Elephant Island

dispositions.rationale: 中文改用常用译名并在首次出现时附英文：沃斯利、怀尔德、欺骗岛、克林、布莱克博罗、麦克尼什、麦卡锡、文森特、詹姆斯·凯尔德号、哈康国王湾，并在涉及字段统一。沃斯利首次出现时注明以领航见长（E8），怀尔德注明留岛主持队伍（E7），不加证据以外的身份。英文同步给出。

evidence.quote: accuracy and quickness as a navigator
I relied upon him to hold the party together while I was away

dispositions.rationale: 英文改为 He decided to call for volunteers，与证据和中文“决定征求”一致。

evidence.quote: I decided to call for volunteers

dispositions.rationale: 把木匠一段改为“另一件事是加固小船”，去掉排在定名单之后造成的先后暗示，也不把木匠与名单中某人对应。

evidence.quote: He first inquired if he was to go with me

dispositions.rationale: 改为“木匠拼凑出的骨架很简陋”，英文同步，没有补写具体材料。

dispositions.rationale: 在“决定做出后”之前补入：三人登上临海岩顶察看冰情，浮冰带看来碎得足够，决定除非条件不允许，次日早晨乘詹姆斯·凯尔德号出发；ev 加入 E30。中英同步。

evidence.quote: I decided that, unless the conditions forbade it, we would make a start in the James Caird on the following morning.

dispositions.rationale: 在 story.8 末尾补入结局：5月8日12点30分麦卡锡望见南乔治亚，距离开象岛整十四天；5月10日驶向被认为是哈康国王湾的海湾，抢风五次进入湾口，转向南岸小湾。没有写登陆，ev 加入 E26、E28。中英同步。

tacking five times in the strong wind
